questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How is the safe bearing capacity of a rock foundation estimated from its uniaxial compressive strength (UCS)?
options: Based on UCS and rock mass quality; safe bearing capacity = UCS / factor of safety
Equal to the UCS with no factor of safety applied
Determined solely from the colour of the freshly exposed rock surface
Governed only by grain size and never by rock mass quality
questions.solution: Based on UCS and rock mass quality; safe bearing capacity = UCS / factor of safety

Temperature of mylonitization from the mineral assemblage in the tails
Vorticity number from the angle between tails and foliation
questions.solution: Shear sense (direction of shear) from the asymmetric tail geometry

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Lateritic nickel deposits (e.g., Goro, Murrin Murrin) form by what process?
options: Intense tropical weathering of ultramafic rocks, concentrating Ni in saprolite and limonite zones
Magmatic sulfide segregation in mantle-derived basaltic magma
Hydrothermal replacement of dolomitic host rocks by Ni carbonates
Vein-type mineralization with Ni sulfides/arsenides in granitic fractures
questions.solution: Intense tropical weathering of ultramafic rocks, concentrating Ni in saprolite and limonite zones

Only the initial strontium isotope composition

questions.solution: Age of the sample and initial ⁸⁷Sr/⁸⁶Sr ratio

options: Decompression during exhumation (garnet becomes unstable and reacts)
Infiltration of hydrothermal fluids along fractures
questions.solution: Decompression during exhumation (garnet becomes unstable and reacts)

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The Cretaceous–Paleogene (K–Pg) mass extinction (~66 Ma) is most strongly linked to which event?
options: Chicxulub asteroid impact (iridium anomaly, 75% species loss including non-avian dinosaurs)
Siberian Traps eruptions at the Permian–Triassic boundary
Central Atlantic Magmatic Province at the Triassic–Jurassic boundary
Eocene Thermal Maximum with deep-sea warming
questions.solution: Chicxulub asteroid impact (iridium anomaly, 75% species loss including non-avian dinosaurs)

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An oxbow lake forms through which fluvial process?
options: River meander cutoff (neck or chute cutoff isolating a meander loop)
Glacial erosion of a bedrock valley
Volcanic dam blocking a river channel
Tectonic subsidence of a graben floor
questions.solution: River meander cutoff (neck or chute cutoff isolating a meander loop)

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A talus cone at the base of a cliff is best described as:
options: An accumulation of fallen rock debris at the cliff base, resting at the angle of repose (35–40°)
A river-deposited alluvial apron on the valley floor
A wind-blown sand dune on the leeward slope
A flat bench of residual soil from in-situ weathering
questions.solution: An accumulation of fallen rock debris at the cliff base, resting at the angle of repose (35–40°)

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The Fry method of strain analysis uses center-to-center distances of grains to determine what?
options: The finite strain ellipse from an initially random grain distribution
The sense of shear from S–C fabric geometry
The vorticity number from porphyroclast asymmetry
The strain ratio from deformed elliptical objects (Rf/φ method)
questions.solution: The finite strain ellipse from an initially random grain distribution

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In the threshold hillslope model, the maximum stable slope angle is primarily controlled by:

The rate of tectonic uplift alone
The rate of fluvial erosion alone
questions.solution: Rock strength and weathering rate (material properties), not just uplift or climate

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge

questions.solution: Fractional crystallization and gravity settling of crystals in a large, long-lived magma chamber

questions.stem: How do P-waves and S-waves differ in particle motion and typical crustal speed?

S-waves travel faster than P-waves but only as surface motion

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which spatial interpolation method weights sample points by inverse distance raised to a power parameter?
options: Spline (exact, smooth surface through all points)

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which seismic wave arrives first at a station, and which wave type causes the most damage?
options: P-wave arrives first; surface waves (Love, Rayleigh) cause the most damage
S-wave arrives first; P-wave causes the most damage
Surface waves arrive first; they are the least damaging
Only one wave type exists, traveling at light speed
questions.solution: P-wave arrives first; surface waves (Love, Rayleigh) cause the most damage

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Peralkaline rhyolite (molar (Na₂O+K₂O)/Al₂O₃ > 1) is characterized by which mineral assemblage?
options: Sodic amphibole (riebeckite), aegirine, alkali feldspar, quartz; no primary muscovite
Calcic plagioclase, augite, hypersthene (metaluminous mafic assemblage)
questions.solution: Sodic amphibole (riebeckite), aegirine, alkali feldspar, quartz; no primary muscovite

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The typical lithological assemblage of the Dharwar Craton comprises:
options: Greenstone belts (volcano-sedimentary) + TTG gneisses + late granites
Massive granites with no supracrustal rocks
questions.solution: Greenstone belts (volcano-sedimentary) + TTG gneisses + late granites

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Sedimentary rock colour: red = hematite (oxidizing), grey = reducing. White colour typically indicates:
options: Leached or very pure composition (clean quartz sandstone, pure limestone, kaolinite)
Iron-rich sediment under strongly reducing conditions
Volcanic ash-rich sediment with ferromagnesian minerals
Organic-rich mudstone with high pyrite and TOC
questions.solution: Leached or very pure composition (clean quartz sandstone, pure limestone, kaolinite)

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Metasomatism refers to a change in rock bulk composition brought about by:
options: Change in mineral assemblage under increasing temperature and pressure
Mechanical deformation producing foliation without any chemical change
Change in bulk composition by fluid transport of elements
Isochemical recrystallization in the solid state under new P-T conditions
questions.solution: Metasomatism: addition/removal of elements. Skarn: Ca-Fe-Mg alteration of carbonate.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In well logging, the sonic tool measures compressional slowness (Δt), which is primarily used to calculate:
options: Compressional slowness Δt (μs/ft). Porosity: ϕ = (Δt - Δt_ma)/(Δt_f - Δt_ma) (Wyllie). Secondary porosity indicator
Formation bulk density measured by gamma-gamma scattering; porosity computed from the matrix and pore fluid densities
Natural radioactivity from potassium, uranium and thorium used as a shale indicator and for correlation
Resistivity of the invaded and virgin zones used to compute water saturation from the Archie equation
questions.solution: Sonic: Δt_ma: 55.5 (ss), 47.5 (ls), 43.5 (dol). Crossplot with density → lithology.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Sedimentary exhalative (SEDEX) deposits form at:
options: On the continental surface in river delta distributary channels
At atmospheric conditions within near-surface karst solution cavities
Exclusively on stable continental shelves far from any volcanic activity
questions.solution: SEDEX: Zn-Pb from hydrothermal fluids on seafloor.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In U-Pb dating of zircon, the two decay schemes used are ²³⁸U→²⁰⁶Pb and ²³⁵U→²⁰⁷Pb, and their results are displayed on a:
options: K-Ar method on potassium feldspar separates from the same rock sample being dated
C-14 method on associated organic matter in the overlying sedimentary beds of the area, for ages up to 50,000 years
²³⁸U → ²⁰⁶Pb (T½ = 4.47 Ga). ²³⁵U → ²⁰⁷Pb (T½ = 704 Ma). Concordia diagram. Discordia = Pb loss
Single isotope method with no isochron or concordia diagram control at all
questions.solution: U-Pb: robust dating. Concordia: both decay systems agree. Discordia: Pb loss event. SHRIMP, LA-ICPMS.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In a plunging anticline eroded to a level surface, the outcrop pattern of beds forms a:
options: V or nose closing in the direction of plunge
A horseshoe pattern opening in the same direction that the fold axis plunges
Straight parallel belts of equal width that curve gently around the fold closure
Identical elliptical outcrops of equal size regardless of the plunge direction
questions.solution: Plunging folds produce V-shaped (zig-zag) outcrops; an anticline's nose points in the plunge direction.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: To extract 5 m³ of coal, 30 m³ of overburden must be removed. The stripping ratio is:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How is the Darcy velocity related to the seepage velocity in a porous medium?
options: v_s = v×n so seepage velocity is always less than Darcy velocity
v_s < v, so seepage velocity is smaller than the Darcy velocity
Both velocities are identical for flow through any porous medium
questions.solution: Darcy velocity: apparent. Seepage velocity: actual through pores. v_s = v/n_e (effective porosity).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What interference colors does quartz typically show in thin section under crossed polars?
options: Black indicating complete extinction in every orientation
Second-order blue typical of very high birefringence
Third-order red characteristic of strongly birefringent minerals
questions.solution: Quartz: low birefringence → grey-white colors under crossed polars. Uniaxial positive.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Erosion rate: universal soil loss equation (USLE): A = R*K*L*S*C*P
options: The model uses rainfall intensity as the only factor controlling annual soil loss
The model predicts soil loss from a fixed constant without considering any measurable factors
R=rainfall erosivity, K=soil erodibility, L=slope length, S=slope steepness
The model considers the slope angle alone as the only factor controlling soil loss
questions.solution: USLE: A=RKLSCP. R: rainfall energy. K: soil type. L,S: topography. C: cover. P: practice.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In radar remote sensing, backscatter strength increases with which surface characteristic relative to the radar wavelength?
options: Surface smoothness relative to the radar wavelength
Increasing radar wavelength while surface stays fixed
Decreasing look angle to the target area
questions.solution: Radar: rough surfaces scatter more energy back.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Landslide remediation: rock bolts provide:
options: Only re-distribution of surface loads by concreting the slope face
Removal of the overburden to reduce the gravitational driving force acting on the entire slope
Active reinforcement by compressing rock mass and increasing frictional resistance
Blanket drainage of all the groundwater by horizontal filter drains
questions.solution: Rock bolts: grouted or mechanical. Passive: resist movement. Active: pre-tensioned to compress.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: For plutonic rocks, the IUGS QAPF diagram uses which four mineral groups?
options: QAPF diagram. Q = quartz, A = alkali feldspar, P = plagioclase, F = feldspathoid
Silica percentage alone, with boundaries fixed at 45, 52, 63 and 69 percent
Texture alone, separating phaneritic, aphanitic, glassy and porphyritic rocks
Colour index alone, dividing rocks into leucocratic, mesocratic and melanocratic
questions.solution: IUGS: QAPF for felsic. Ultramafic: olivine-pyroxene-hornblende. Volcanic: TAS diagram.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which minerals are most commonly produced by the precipitation of evaporites?
options: Quartz, feldspar and rock fragments transported and deposited by rivers
Carbonate grains of biological origin, including ooids and shell fragments
Clay minerals and silt that accumulated in quiet deep-marine basins
questions.solution: Evaporites: form in restricted basins (high evaporation). Economic: salt, plaster.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Borehole logging: sonic (acoustic) log Δt:
options: Formation resistivity corrected for invasion and borehole diameter
Direct reading of seismic velocity in m/s with no travel time measurement
Slowness (μs/ft) inversely related to velocity. Porosity indicator
Records magnetic susceptibility to detect iron rich horizons
questions.solution: Sonic: Δt = 1/V. Wyllie equation: porosity from Δt. Compaction correction needed.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Given the outcrop positions and elevations of three points on a plane, what structural attitude can be determined?
options: Estimate the throw of a fault from the vertical separation measured at its surface trace
Calculate the fold interlimb angle from the orientation of two measured limb surfaces
Determine strike and dip from three outcrop points. Elevation differences
Locate the outcrop trace of a formation from borehole intersections at three well sites
questions.solution: Three-point: graphical or algebraic. Strike from equal elevation points. Dip from elevation difference.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What distinguishes the water table of an unconfined aquifer from the potentiometric surface of a confined aquifer?
options: Water table is the head surface of the confined aquifer at depth in the area
Potentiometric surface is the phreatic surface of an unconfined aquifer system
Water table is always higher than the potentiometric surface within a drainage basin
Water table: phreatic surface (unconfined). Potentiometric: head in confined aquifer
questions.solution: Water table: actual water level in unconfined aquifer. Potentiometric: imaginary surface in confined aquifer.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In GIS spatial analysis, what does overlay involve when combining two or more geographic data layers, including for suitability studies?
options: Intersection of multiple layers. Weighted overlay for suitability
A union of all the layers, without applying any attribute weighting scheme
A simple map display of only a single raster layer at any one particular time
Visual comparison of the layers by eye, without carrying out any computation
questions.solution: Overlay: slope + geology + land use for site suitability. Boolean or fuzzy logic.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the age and stratigraphic subdivision of the Vindhyan Basin of peninsular India?
options: Mesozoic (Triassic-Jurassic) rift basin filled with coal-bearing fluvial sediments of the Gondwana type
Proterozoic (~1.7-0.5 Ga). Largest Proterozoic basin in India. Semri + Kaimur + Rewa + Bhander
Archean (3.4-2.5 Ga) greenstone-granite terrain of the northern Indian Shield basement rocks
Paleozoic (Cambrian-Permian) shelf basin with rich marine fossil assemblages of brachiopods
questions.solution: Vindhyan: undeformed/thrusted margins. Bhander: stromatolitic limestone. Son Valley.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A bed dipping at 60° shows a width of 20 m across a horizontal surface. Its true (perpendicular) thickness is about:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which option correctly describes the terrain and processes that produce badland topography on soft rocks?
options: Intense gully erosion in soft rocks (shale, clay). High drainage density. Steep slopes, rapid erosion rates
Uniform removal of a thin layer of soil across an entire hillslope by unchannelled sheet overland flow during heavy rainstorms
Terrain dominated by the dissolution of soluble carbonate rocks such as limestone producing sinkholes, caves and underground drainage systems
Erosion by numerous small closely spaced channels that are readily removed by normal ploughing in the following cultivation season
questions.solution: Badlands: South Dakota, Spiti Valley. Land use limitation. Gully rehabilitation needed.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What distinguishes red beds from gray beds in terms of depositional oxidation conditions?
options: Red: pyrite framboids in a reducing environment. Gray: hematite coating on grains
Red: hematite coating (oxidizing). Gray: pyrite/organic matter (reducing)
Red: iron sulfide and organic matter. Gray: hematite and other ferric oxides
Red: reducing conditions with pyrite. Gray: oxidizing conditions with hematite
questions.solution: Red beds: continental (fluvial, aeolian). Gray: marine or deltaic. Diagenetic color.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: According to the Strahler ordering system, how is the order of a stream segment determined as tributaries join downstream?
options: Headwaters = order 1. Two of same order → next order. Mainstream = highest order
Shreve method: at a junction the stream order equals the sum of the two upstream contributing orders
Hack method: every link in the network is assigned an order of magnitude one
Horton method: order one streams join to form order two, order two to form order three
questions.solution: Strahler: no increase at confluence of different orders. Bifurcation ratio: R_b = N_u/N_{u+1}.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What characteristics make an organic-rich (black) shale a potential hydrocarbon source rock?
options: High TOC (>2%). Reducing conditions. Hydrocarbon source rock
High TOC (>2%) but formed exclusively under oxidizing, well-oxygenated conditions
Formed only in freshwater lakes, with no organic carbon or pyrite preservation
Oxidizing conditions with low TOC, rich in hematite and ferric iron minerals
questions.solution: Black shale: anoxic. Pyrite framboids. Total organic carbon. Barnett, Marcellus shales.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Q-system formula: Q = (RQD/Jn)×(Jr/Ja)×(Jw/SRF). For RQD=75, Jn=12, Jr=1.5, Ja=2, Jw=1, SRF=1:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which geological factors are most critical for tunnel design?
options: Rock mass quality, groundwater inflow, swelling/squeezing ground, gas
Only the tunnel length and the number of cross-passages to be driven in the heading
Only the availability of muck disposal space near the portal area
Only the rock strength as measured in the laboratory on dry cores
questions.solution: Tunnels: avoid fault zones. TBM vs drill-and-blast. Rock support: bolts, shotcrete, steel.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal seam covers 2 km², is 2 m thick, with density 1.4 t/m³. The in-situ reserve is about:
questions.solution: Reserve = area×thickness×density = 2×10⁶ m²×2 m×1.4 t/m³ ≈ 5.6 Mt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An upward-arching fold, with the oldest beds in its core, is called a(n):
questions.solution: An anticline arches upward; its limbs dip away from the axis and oldest rocks lie in the core.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal seam covers 5 km², is 5 m thick, with density 1.4 t/m³. The in-situ reserve is about:
questions.solution: Reserve = area×thickness×density = 5×10⁶ m²×5 m×1.4 t/m³ ≈ 35 Mt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How is the apparent dip of a plane calculated from its true dip and the angle between the strike and the section plane?
options: tan α = tan δ · cos θ. α = apparent dip, δ = true dip, θ = angle between the strike line and the section
tan α = sin δ · tan θ. α = apparent dip, δ = true dip, θ = angle between strike and the section
tan α = cos δ · tan θ. α = apparent dip, δ = true dip, θ = the plunge angle of the section line
tan α = tan δ · sin θ. α = apparent dip, δ = true dip, θ = angle between strike and section
questions.solution: Apparent dip is always ≤ true dip. Used for cross-sections not perpendicular to strike.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the colour of the streak produced by the mineral hematite on a streak plate?
questions.solution: Hematite (Fe2O3) — reddish streak. Important iron ore.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Darcy's law states that groundwater discharge is proportional to the hydraulic gradient and the:
options: Porosity of the medium through which the water flows
Specific yield of the aquifer being drained at the time
Temperature of the water flowing through the medium
questions.solution: Q = K·i·A; flow rises with hydraulic conductivity K and gradient i.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Flinn diagram: K = (R-1)/(R-1) where R = axial ratios. K>1 indicates:
options: Oblate (pancake-shaped) fabric indicating that flattening strain is dominant over elongation
Plane strain in which the intermediate principal strain axis is not deformed
Flattening strain with the greatest shortening along the maximum principal stress direction
questions.solution: K>1: elongation dominant (L-tectonite). K<1: flattening dominant (S-tectonite). K=1: plane strain.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: On the Mohs scale of hardness, the hardest mineral (value 10) is:
questions.solution: Mohs scale runs from talc (1) to diamond (10), the hardest natural mineral.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A rock retains 50% of its original parent isotope (half-life 4.47 Gyr). Its radiometric age is about:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: During strong seismic shaking, the soil liquefaction hazard is greatest in which of the following ground conditions?
options: Densely packed gravel with good drainage
Dry clay with low moisture content
Massive solid rock with few discontinuities
questions.solution: Liquefaction: saturated loose sand loses strength during shaking. High water table + loose sand + earthquake = high risk.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which geological conditions are most important when selecting a dam site?
options: Foundation on thick alluvial gravel with a high seepage gradient below
Uniform flat-lying shale beds with a weak shear zone along the foundation
Foundation on competent rock, watertight abutments, no active faults
Reservoir site underlain by soluble gypsum and anhydrite formations
questions.solution: Dam: avoid karst (leakage), shears, soluble rocks. Grout curtain for seepage.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes an arroyo and the environment in which it develops?
options: Steep-walled, flat-floored ephemeral channel in arid regions. Incised
Channel that carries flowing water continuously throughout the entire year without drying
Broad valley with steep walls and a flat floor carved by glacial ice
Multiple unstable channels that split and rejoin around mid-channel bars
questions.solution: Arroyo: incision by base level fall or climate change. SW USA. Valley fill.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Back-arc basin formation: extension behind volcanic arc:
options: Caused by collision of a continental fragment with the volcanic arc
Caused by ridge subduction and the opening of a slab window beneath the arc
Caused by crustal thickening due to compressional forces at the margin
Caused by rollback of subducting slab or mantle wedge convection
questions.solution: Back-arc: Sea of Japan, Philippine Sea. Extension: graben, new ocean floor. Volcanic arc on upper plate.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Specific gravity of gold is approximately:
questions.solution: Gold SG = 19.3. Very heavy. Gravity separation effective.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How many cleavage directions and at what angle does the mineral calcite cleave?
options: Perfect cleavage producing thin elastic sheets
Three directions of cleavage at right angles
A single direction of cleavage parallel to the base
questions.solution: Calcite (CaCO3) — double refraction. Effervesces in dilute HCl.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is shotcrete and how is it applied in underground construction?
options: Concrete cast in timber formwork and cured for twenty-eight days before any loading
Precast panels bolted onto the rock face with no bonding material at all
Sprayed concrete (dry or wet mix). Steel fiber reinforced. Applied to rock surface
Poured tremie concrete placed underwater through a tremie delivery pipe
questions.solution: Shotcrete: immediate support. Add accelerator. Wire mesh or fiber. 50-100mm thick.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: When multiple wells are pumped close together, well interference leads to:
options: A single well lowers the water level only within its own circle of influence
Multiple wells → cone superposition. Additional drawdown. Reduced yield
Pumping one well raises the water level in all neighbouring wells
Interference appears only when the wells are tapping different aquifers
questions.solution: Interference: s_total = Σs_i. Spacing wells to minimize. Constant rate vs constant drawdown.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Garnet porphyroblast with inclusion trail (Si/Se) indicates:
options: Timing of growth relative to deformation
Composition of the surrounding country rock
Rate of cooling following peak metamorphism
questions.solution: Inclusion trails: show garnet grew during folding. Rotational vs non-rotational help determine syn-kinematic growth.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: To which crystal system does quartz, one of the most common minerals, belong?
questions.solution: Quartz: SiO2, hexagonal prisms terminated by pyramids. Piezoelectric.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What characteristics should a good index (guide) fossil possess?
options: Widespread but short-lived in geologic time
Rare and confined to a single basin with an extremely long stratigraphic range
Found in igneous and metamorphic rocks, permitting absolute-age dating of plutons
Geographically restricted to one locality but present in almost every rock formation there
questions.solution: Wide distribution plus a short time range makes a fossil useful for correlation/dating.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Inertinite macerals in coal originate from which type of plant material?
options: Fresh unaltered plant tissue preserved in the peat before burial and decay
Spore exines rich in waxy cuticular material of the original plant
Algal remains deposited in marine basins and their transformation products
Oxidized or charred plant material (fusain, charcoal)
questions.solution: Inertinite: fusinite, semifusinite, micrinite. High carbon, low volatile. May be wildfire products.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the origin and composition of an esker in a glaciated landscape?
options: Ridge of stratified sand/gravel deposited by subglacial stream
Circular depression formed when a block of ice buried in outwash melts
Broad plain of stratified sand and gravel spread beyond the glacier margin
Gentle undulating plain of unsorted debris deposited directly by glacier ice
questions.solution: Esker: sinuous ridge. Glaciofluvial. Useful aggregate resource.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which spaceborne sensor carries OLI and TIRS instruments and has a 16-day revisit and a 185 km swath?
options: Landsat 8: OLI (9 bands, 30m) + TIRS (2 thermal, 100m). 16-day revisit. 185km swath
Landsat 8: carries only a single panchromatic band at 15m, and has no thermal capability
Landsat 8: 36 spectral bands at 250m resolution, offering a daily revisit period
Landsat 8: 13 bands, 10m resolution, a 5-day revisit period and a 290km swath
questions.solution: Landsat: 1972-2023. OLI bands: coastal, blue, green, red, NIR, SWIR1, SWIR2, pan (15m), cirrus.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) produces a 2D or 3D subsurface image by measuring:
options: 2D/3D resistivity imaging. Dipole-dipole, Wenner, Schlumberger arrays. For contamination, cavity, archaeology
One dimensional vertical electrical sounding with the current electrodes expanded about a single fixed centre point of the spread
Mapping of magnetic susceptibility contrasts for locating buried ferrous metallic objects
Measurement of natural electric and magnetic fields at the surface to image deep crustal resistivity
questions.solution: ERT: multi-electrode. Pseudo-section. Inversion. Time-lapse ERT for process monitoring.
